subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to dropped-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion, or should this issue define the host-local root policy for `MEDIA:` replies?
rationale: The current behavior is both a UX/debugging bug and a security-sensitive file-read policy boundary, so automation should not choose a broader host-local root contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
options.body: Fix this issue by adding reason-specific warn logs and optional user-facing failure text, while keeping root expansion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or a merged shared-root design.

options.title: Adopt A Shared Root Policy
options.body: Use this issue only after maintainers approve a shared media/filesystem root contract such as `tools.fs.roots`, with upgrade and security proof.

options.title: Document Managed Roots Only
options.body: Keep the secure current boundary and close only after docs and diagnostics make unsupported absolute paths obvious to operators.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
recommendation.body: Fix this issue by adding reason-specific warn logs and optional user-facing failure text, while keeping root expansion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or a merged shared-root design.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the current outbound media policy and access-plumbing history.
